//: TEMPLATE, not a live settings file. Rendered into each agent account's own ~/.claude/office.settings.json by packages/server/src/features/orchestrator/provision.ts (run it through scripts/provision-user.sh). Do NOT add hook entries here: drop a fragment into config/hooks/fragments/ instead — see that directory's .gitkeep. Placeholders ${EVENT_SERVER_ORIGIN}, ${HOOK_INGEST_TOKEN}, ${CA_CERT_PATH}, ${REPO_ROOT}, ${USER_HOME} and ${TARGET_USER} are substituted at provision time; an unknown ${...} is a hard error, never an empty string. On permissions.defaultMode: 'manual' is the one mode that still raises permission prompts. On 2.1.283 --permission-mode takes acceptEdits|auto|bypassPermissions|manual|dontAsk|plan, `auto` is now the CLI default, and auto/dontAsk/bypassPermissions all resolve permissions without asking — which silently removes the PermissionRequest hook the design uses to mark an agent blocked in the UI. In this settings key the canonical spelling is 'default' with 'manual' an accepted alias for it (checked against the installed build's own schema); 'manual' is written because the word 'default' in a config file now means `auto`, the opposite of what the line is for. On permissions.allow: it names the office's OWN MCP servers and nothing else. MCP tool calls require permission approval, so in manual mode an unlisted claim_task raises a PermissionRequest and parks the desk waiting for a human to approve every claim — which is not an office (spike 003 §6). The rule syntax has a trap: an allow rule's SERVER segment must be glob-free, so the rule `mcp__*` is skipped with a warning and auto-approves NOTHING while looking permissive. It IS valid as a deny rule; the asymmetry is the trap. A mcp__ rule containing parentheses is dropped entirely, so there is no parameter matching here — `mcp__office_tasks__claim_task(task_id:*)` is not a rule, it is a silently discarded line. Every entry below must therefore name a server this office actually configures in agents/<role>.md. This does NOT weaken the PermissionRequest-marks-the-agent-blocked model, which exists for file writes and shell commands, not for the office's own coordination calls. mcp__office_session__* is listed before ticket 018 serves it on purpose: an allow rule for a server that is not attached matches nothing, whereas discovering the rule is missing costs a parked desk.
